title: Rigveda 4.40: To Dadhikra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 4.40: To Dadhikra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 4.40 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Dadhikra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 4, the family book of Vāmadeva. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 301r-302r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>da̱dhi̱krāvṇa̱ id u̱ nu ca̍rkirāma̱ viśvā̱ in mām u̱ṣasa̍ḥ sūdayantu | a̱pām a̱gner u̱ṣasa̱ḥ sūrya̍sya̱ bṛha̱spate̍r āṅgira̱sasya̍ ji̱ṣṇoḥ ||
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>LET us recite the praise of Dadhikrâvan: may all the Mornings move me to exertion; Praise of the Lord of Waters, Dawn, and Agni, Br̥ihaspati Son of Angiras, and Sûrya.

translation.original_ref: RV 4.40.2-4 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 7, varga 14); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 301v
translation.original_text:
2satvā̍ bhari̱ṣo ga̍vi̱ṣo du̍vanya̱sac chra̍va̱syād i̱ṣa u̱ṣasa̍s turaṇya̱sat | sa̱tyo dra̱vo dra̍va̱raḥ pa̍taṁga̱ro da̍dhi̱krāveṣa̱m ūrja̱ṁ sva̍r janat ||
3u̱ta smā̍sya̱ drava̍tas turaṇya̱taḥ pa̱rṇaṁ na ver anu̍ vāti praga̱rdhina̍ḥ | śye̱nasye̍va̱ dhraja̍to aṅka̱sam pari̍ dadhi̱krāvṇa̍ḥ sa̱horjā tari̍trataḥ ||
4u̱ta sya vā̱jī kṣi̍pa̱ṇiṁ tu̍raṇyati grī̱vāyā̍m ba̱ddho a̍pika̱kṣa ā̱sani̍ | kratu̍ṁ dadhi̱krā anu̍ sa̱ṁtavī̍tvat pa̱thām aṅkā̱ṁsy anv ā̱panī̍phaṇat ||
translation.text:
2Brave, seeking war and booty, dwelling with the good and with the swift, may he hasten the food of Dawn. May he the true, the fleet, the lover of the course, the bird-like Dadhikrâvan, bring food, strength, and light.
3His pinion, rapid runner, fans him m his way, as of a bird that hastens onward to its aim, And, as it were a falcon's gliding through the air, strikes Dadhikrâvan's side as he speeds on with might.
4Bound by the neck and by the flanks and by the mouth, the vigorous Courser lends new swiftness to his speed. Drawing himself together, as his strength allows, Dadhikrâs springs along the windings of the paths.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 301v (numbered 110v by the scribe) (OPenn image 302, upper leaf). The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 302r (numbered 111r by the scribe), begins in RV 4.40.5 ‹-ṛtam›. Verses 4.40.2-4 end on this page.

translation.original_text: <sup>5</sup>ha̱ṁsaḥ śu̍ci̱ṣad vasu̍r antarikṣa̱sad dhotā̍ vedi̱ṣad ati̍thir duroṇa̱sat | nṛ̱ṣad va̍ra̱sad ṛ̍ta̱sad vyo̍ma̱sad a̱bjā go̱jā ṛ̍ta̱jā a̍dri̱jā ṛ̱tam ||
translation.text: <sup>5</sup>The Hamsa homed in light, the Vasu in mid-air, the priest beside the altar, in the house the guest, Dweller in noblest place, mid men, in truth, in sky, born of flood, kine, truth, mountain, he is holy Law.
